source.title: Stochastic Gradient Methods with Block Diagonal Matrix Adaptation
source.authors: Jihun Yun; A. Lozano; Eunho Yang

record.file_problem: none; full paper and supplementary material are present
record.tranche_reason: Its optimizer comparisons refine the claim: diagonal Adam has higher CIFAR test error than SGD, while spectrum-clipped block Adam has lower error.
record.gate_note: The paper compares test performance across optimizers. It does not test random-label memorization, width sweeps, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, dropout, sharpness measures, or example removal. Figure-only MNIST and language-model comparisons are described qualitatively; no exact values are reconstructed from plots.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out performance of adaptive optimizers and momentum SGD. Its CIFAR results reproduce the diagonal Adam disadvantage and show that changing the adaptive update and adding spectrum clipping can remove it, bearing on V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors conclude that block-diagonal adaptation improves convergence and can improve generalization, and that spectrum clipping produces strong benchmark performance by approaching SGD-like updates. Qualify the language-model result: clipped Block-Adam achieves similar perplexity to GGT, rather than outperforming it.
record.recipe_differences: Compares diagonal and block-diagonal adaptive optimizers, SGD, and GGT; introduces spectrum clipping. It does not reproduce the optimizer comparisons described in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset changes the relative performance of AMSBound versus SGD; CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 results differ.

fits_no_version.finding: On MNIST, block Adam and block RMSProp have more stable and generally superior test accuracy than their diagonal counterparts; these experiments provide no SGD comparator.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Block-diagonal adaptation can improve stability and held-out accuracy relative to diagonal adaptation.

fits_no_version.finding: Block Adam improves the beta-TCVAE disentanglement MIG score except at beta = 8.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer structure affects learned representation disentanglement.

record.problems: CIFAR test-error table reports no uncertainty. The paper gives qualitative generalization comparisons for MNIST and language modeling from figures without exact values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant numeric table results left out. Figure-only qualitative comparisons are not added as rows because exact values are not stated.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
A controlled comparison establishing the convolutional advantage or the contribution of local connectivity.

A systematic limited-versus-broader tuning comparison; decoupled weight decay; an explicit Adam-to-SGD switching comparison; and quantitative matching of training performance alongside the tabulated CIFAR errors. PTB held-out performance is tested qualitatively, not untested.
Held-out performance across batch sizes with fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout addition, removal, strength, or interactions with training-set size and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap correlations, and comparisons with norm or margin measures.
Removal of memorized examples compared with random removal.

missing.what: Add the qualitative PTB held-out comparison: spectrum-clipped Block-Adam achieves similar test perplexity to GGT and outperforms the other compared optimizers. The omission is acknowledged in rows_left_out, but a qualitative row is needed to represent this V4 verdict; exact plot values are unnecessary.
missing.locator: Section 5, Language Models; Figure 5(b); Appendix C

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4. Table 1 reports no uncertainty, so small numerical differences should not be described as statistically established. Tuning includes recommended or searched learning rates, fixed Adam decay parameters, a larger numerical-stability parameter, and extra clipping parameters for the proposed method; this is not a controlled test of tuning breadth. The supplied manuscript identifies itself as a preprint under review, so the record's ICLR peer-review attribution is unsupported.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same recipe.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local connectivity.
Language-model and broader benchmark comparisons are figure-only; no specific training-performance values are reported alongside the CIFAR test errors.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
